purpose: Prevent the corpus from turning bedside practice into pressure, advice, blame, spectacle, countdowns, or generic euphemism.

standards.name: May, not must
standards.rule: Use possibility language for hearing, awareness, timing, and meaning unless the source specifically supports stronger wording.

standards.name: No guilt syntax
standards.rule: Do not imply family failure around feeding, presence, missed moments, touch, calls, or exact timing.

standards.name: No instruction by implication
standards.rule: When naming a care move, explicitly state that local assessment, care plan, clinician, funeral, legal, or tradition guidance controls the action.

standards.name: Body dignity before body detail
standards.rule: Name bodily changes plainly, but do not make body fluids, smell, skin, eyes, or after-death care lurid.

standards.name: Jurisdiction humility
standards.rule: Any after-death call, verification, certification, registration, coroner, funeral, or equipment guidance must be localised or quarantined.

standards.name: No last-words fetish
standards.rule: Do not imply that a meaningful final sentence is normal, owed, or necessary. Silence and ordinary speech are valid witnessed moments.

standards.name: Symbolic language is not prophecy
standards.rule: Home, travel, visitors, timing-like speech, or symbolic fragments may be recorded, but must not be rendered as exact prediction, diagnosis, or spiritual proof.

standards.name: Scripts are invitations, never duties
standards.rule: Goodbye, forgiveness, love, thanks, apology, or permission language must be presented only as possible language that may or may not fit the relationship.

standards.name: Clarity without language policing
standards.rule: Use clear language when understanding or safety requires it, while preserving personal, cultural, faith, or family language when ethically quoted or summarized.

standards.name: Names and kinship words are identifying
standards.rule: Names, kinship roles, and distinctive last words require high de-identification and consent review before any public use.

standards.name: DNR/DNACPR does not mean do-not-care
standards.rule: Any code-status rendering must name care that continues and avoid abandonment language.

standards.name: Comfort language must not hide treatment changes
standards.rule: Comfort-focused terms must distinguish continued care from limits or withdrawal of specific interventions.

standards.name: Jurisdiction-locked terms stay locked
standards.rule: POLST/MOLST/DNACPR/MAID/VSED/advance-directive terms must not be generalized beyond source jurisdiction or care context.

standards.name: Donation language must avoid heroic coercion
standards.rule: Organ-donation and honor-walk language must not rank donor deaths above non-donor deaths or pressure authorization.

standards.name: No grief policing
standards.rule: Do not imply that grief has a correct timeline, stage sequence, performance, or endpoint.

standards.name: Aftermath is not a checklist
standards.rule: First-days records may name calls, papers, funeral terms, and administrative burdens, but must route specific actions to local/professional authority.

standards.name: Objects identify households
standards.rule: Clothes, rings, rooms, pets, photographs, and belongings require heightened consent and de-identification before private accounts enter.

standards.name: Children are not publication material
standards.rule: Child words, drawings, attendance choices, and reactions remain high-gate unless guardian consent, child-safeguarding review, and identifiability review all pass.

standards.name: Tradition terms are not generic comfort language
standards.rule: Keep sacred and community-specific terms intact, with aliases for search only; do not translate them into generic spiritual reassurance or use them as aesthetic decoration.

rev0012_perspective_axis_note: Public rendering must distinguish witness role, account type, authority boundary, and missing perspectives before clinical, setting, or practice interpretation.
